name: Fine-tuning Gemma 3 270M IT as a small proofreader in front of Stanza + frozen UD rules (datasets/proofing, role proofreader)
registered_by: proofreader-training-agent (owner approval of 2026-09-29 night, status/journal.jsonl 2026-09-29T21:37:26.749Z and 2026-09-29T21:39:19.620Z)
owner_request: Once datasets/proofing is finished and qualified, train ONE small model to see whether it helps SymbolicLM; base model Gemma3-270M (Qwen3-0.6B judged too slow for CPU). Scoped to this experiment only: fine-tuning google/gemma-3-270m-it on datasets/proofing. No other training.
frozen_before_results: Written before any optimizer step of this run and before any prediction of the fine-tuned checkpoint on any split. The zero-shot reference numbers for gemma3-270m:proof and qwen3-1.7b:proof already exist (eval/reports/current/proofing/report.md, pilot stage s300 and the full formalizer-v1 pool respectively) and are read but not altered by this preregistration; qwen3-0.6b:proof and the fine-tuned model are scored fresh, after this file is frozen.
question: Does fine-tuning Gemma 3 270M IT on datasets/proofing turn it from a zero-shot-harmful rewriter (report.md s300: net -3.0) into a net-positive proofreader on the sealed proofing test, without breaking rows that already parse, and how does it compare to much larger untrained references?

hypotheses.H1: The fine-tuned checkpoint reaches strict-oracle net_delta > 0 on eval/suites/proofing/test.jsonl (paired cluster bootstrap 95% CI excludes 0), always-on (no gate).
hypotheses.H2: The fine-tuned checkpoint's break rate on already-passing sealed-test rows (kind identity, or any row whose raw_oracle.strict is true) is <= 1% (Wilson 95% upper bound), matching the owner's break-rate priority (report.md, dataset_rules).
hypotheses.H3: The fine-tuned checkpoint's net_delta is higher than the untrained gemma3-270m:proof zero-shot baseline's net_delta on the same sealed-test rows, by a margin whose CI excludes 0 (report.md's zero-shot gemma3-270m:proof pilot number, net -3.0, is expected to be reversed by fine-tuning: H4 of report.md's own ceiling analysis put the input-noise-repairable ceiling at 22.2% of failing rows, so a positive but modest net_delta, not near that ceiling, is expected).
hypotheses.H4: Gating to gate_no_spacy keeps most of the always-on repair benefit at a break rate no higher than always-on (directional replication of report.md §2c on the fine-tuned model, not assumed).
hypotheses.non_claim: This run does not attempt to show the fine-tuned 270M model beats the untrained Qwen3-1.7B reference (6x the parameters); a result either way is reported, not treated as a proxy for size scaling beyond this one pair.

arms.name: no_rewrite
arms.source: each sealed-test row's own raw_oracle (already computed at rules v1.4 when the corpus was built)

arms.name: gemma3-270m:proof (untrained, zero-shot)
arms.kind: reference, scored fresh on the sealed test
arms.note: report.md's s300 pilot number (net -3.0) is a different, disjoint sample (pilot rows are excluded from the sealed test by construction); this arm re-scores the same untrained base on the sealed test itself for a same-rows comparison

arms.name: qwen3-0.6b:proof (untrained, zero-shot)
arms.kind: reference, scored fresh on the sealed test
arms.note: no full-corpus run exists for this candidate (only a disjoint s300 pilot sample); scored fresh because the same-test-rows result does not already exist

arms.name: qwen3-1.7b:proof (untrained, zero-shot)
arms.kind: reference, reused from an existing result on the same rows
arms.note: report.md §2b scored this candidate on the FULL formalizer-v1 train+dev pool at rules v1.4 (break 0.8%, repair 12.5%, net +6.3); the sealed proofing test is a subset of that pool (test rows are formalizer-v1 dev rows outside the pilot), so its cached per-id oracle results (tools/research/proofing.mjs CACHE) are filtered to the sealed-test ids rather than re-run, honoring 'from existing results where the same test rows are scored'

changed_factor: Whether the base is fine-tuned on datasets/proofing (arm 5) versus zero-shot at three sizes (arms 2-4); arm 1 is the no-rewrite floor. This is a single training arm, not a base-size sweep: Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B are untrained references only (owner scope, journal 2026-09-29T21:39:19.620Z), never fine-tuning candidates in this run.

data.data_version: proofing VERSION counter 2 (manifest 71366400...), following the 2026-09-30 rename of the training-ready projection from the workaround role name 'formalizer' to the proper role 'proofreader' (training/cli.mjs role(), training/python/train.py --role, and the qualification() schema were extended the same day; no row content changed, only paths)
data.sealed_test: eval/suites/proofing/test.jsonl (1,135 rows: identity 518, repair 142, hard 475; sha256 1fd35e1a3c964d1138fbc59a588a7957b48729ef8ea03cc374b8a1efda68ec8d); never read by training, dev selection, or the qualification record
data.oracle: tools/research/proofing-oracle.mjs (frozen-rules-v1.4, Stanza + lib/ud-to-sop, SHA256SUMS-checked copy; eval/run.mjs execution equivalence against the sealed row's SOURCE formalizer-v1 gold, looked up by source_id): strict = execution_equivalent, tolerant = execution_equivalent_tolerant. The evaluator reuses tools/research/proofing-oracle.mjs's exported oracle()/scoreRows() and tools/research/proofing.mjs's exported checks()/charEdit()/bootstrap(); a new evaluation script (tools/research/proofing-eval-checkpoint.mjs) is added for this run because the existing CLI (generate/score commands) is scoped to formalizer-v1 pilot stages, not the sealed test.

recipe_policy.mode: LoRA adapter (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05; config/train-gemma.json lr 2e-4), not --full
recipe_policy.justification: This is a single exploratory arm answering 'does fine-tuning help at all', not a base-size or full-vs-adapter comparison (unlike formalizer-size-v1, which used --full to remove LoRA rank as a confound across four different bases). LoRA is far cheaper on this small, low-diversity corpus (6,095 rows, p99 total tokens 87) and the recipe already ships tuned rank/alpha/dropout for Gemma 3 270M.
recipe_policy.batch: batch_size 2 x gradient_accumulation 8 = 16 sequences per optimizer step

budget.checkpoint_cadence: latest and (dev-loss-gated) best at each epoch end (training/python/train.py: for role != formalizer, best is written only when dev loss improves over the previous best)
budget.selection: best is the epoch with the lowest development loss (dev loss is diagnostic-only for a non-formalizer role, DS007; no SOP execution-equivalence selection applies to a text-target role). The sealed test is never used for selection.
budget.attempts: one run per this preregistration; at most one --resume of the same identity for a staged early-stopping check or an infrastructure interruption
budget.abort_conditions: non-finite loss, OOM or cgroup OOM kill, controller resource floors, wall-time cap of 120 minutes
budget.gpu_policy: one GPU-intensive worker on the machine (checked via nvidia-smi and models/.training.lock before the run; free at registration time)

early_stopping.mechanism: train.py's own interim-check/early-stop loop only fires for role formalizer (it scores a generated SOP with eval/run.mjs) and this recipe does not set interim_check_rows, so it is a no-op either way; the equivalent check for a text-target role is done EXTERNALLY, in two stages, because train.py cannot pause mid-run to invoke a different oracle: (1) `train --max-steps 381` (~1 epoch), stop; (2) evaluate the resulting checkpoint's dev loss and a greedy decode of a stratified 100-row sample of datasets/proofing/proofreader/dev.jsonl (proportional by kind x language, seed 20260930), scored by the proofing oracle; (3) `train --resume` (no step cap) for the remaining budget only if the stage-1 check does not trip the stopping rule below.
early_stopping.stopping_rule: After epoch 1: stop and keep the epoch-1 checkpoint if the 100-row dev sample shows break_rate (share of already-oracle-passing sampled rows the checkpoint now fails) > 10%, or if the checkpoint shows identity collapse (zero rows actually rewritten, i.e. every output equals its input, on the repair-kind rows of the sample) or degenerate output (more than 20% empty/capped generations). Otherwise continue to the full 3-epoch budget.
early_stopping.decision_rule: The run is judged a success worth keeping/merging into SymbolicLM's optional rewrite hook only if H1 and H2 both hold on the sealed test (net_delta CI excludes 0 above zero, and break rate Wilson upper bound <= 1%); H3/H4 are reported regardless of outcome, not gating.

evaluation.checkpoint: best (lowest dev loss), merged with training/cli.mjs merge --role proofreader --checkpoint best
evaluation.predictions: raw HF/transformers greedy decode of the merged checkpoint, message-only prompt (tok.apply_chat_template([{role:user,content:row.input}]), no system role, no instruction wrapper — matching the training prompt exactly, unlike the zero-shot candidates' proof-prompt wrapper) via a new script (training/python/generate_causal.py), then GGUF Q8_0 (llama.cpp) after verifying the export reproduces the transformers greedy output on 50 rows
evaluation.metrics: break rate (Wilson 95% CI) on already-passing rows, repair rate (Wilson 95% CI) on already-failing rows, net_delta (paired cluster bootstrap 95% CI, clusters = semantic_case_id, 10,000 resamples seed 7 — tools/research/proofing.mjs bootstrap()), meaning-preservation checks (tools/research/proofing.mjs checks()), identity share, by language (en only: the sealed test is EN-only per report.md §5) and by gate (always-on vs gate_no_spacy from each row's signals.gate_no_spacy)
evaluation.cpu_speed: GGUF Q8_0 via llama-server on this host, ms/message and tok/s on 30-50 real proofing messages (protocol matching report.md §6's untrained-base measurement, for a fair before/after comparison)
evaluation.gpu_bulk_eval: llama-server GPU, prompt cache off (cache_prompt false); reproducibility verified on 100 rows (repeat run, identical outputs) before trusting the GGUF sealed-test number over the raw-transformers number

non_goals: no rule changes to lib/ud-to-sop; no tuning on the sealed test; no fine-tuning of any model other than gemma3-270m; no change to SymbolicLM's default behavior without evidence from this run

deviations.before: the epoch-1 early-stopping check was already run and passed
deviations.what: podman.mjs's default 48 GiB CUDA-driver-free floor failed 3 times before the first preflight (measured free 34.3-34.8 GiB of 128 GiB total) although nvidia-smi showed 0% GPU utilization and no other GPU consumer; the GB10 unified-memory driver figure excludes reclaimable page cache (host MemAvailable 113 GiB), the exact caveat train.py already documents. Used the tool's own bounded, documented override (TRAIN_MIN_CUDA_FREE_GIB=24, within its accepted 8..48 range and below the measured free figure; TRAIN_CUDA_FREE_CHECK=host so the per-step guard relies on the 113 GiB MemAvailable floor) rather than any cache reclamation; no qualification or authorization gate was touched.

deviations.before: the stage-1 (epoch 1) checkpoint scored net +0.23 [0.15,0.32] on the 100-row dev sample, decision: continue
deviations.what: The early_stopping.mechanism section's staged '--max-steps 381 then --resume for the rest' plan does not work as written: training/cli.mjs's --resume requires the exact same --max-steps value as the original invocation (part of the frozen run identity, runManifest()), so a run capped at 381 steps cannot be resumed with a larger cap to reach epoch 2-3 under the same run identity. Since the stage-1 check already passed and one epoch costs about 180 seconds on this GPU, the run was restarted cleanly (no --max-steps; the recipe's own epochs=3 gives total=1143) rather than fought through --resume; the stage-1 numbers above stand as the recorded early-stopping check, the discarded stage-1 checkpoint is not otherwise used.
